properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 16 at 12:47PM PST until November 16 at 1:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
TORMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
West Central Santa Cruz County in northern California...

* Until 130 PM PST.

* At 1247 PM PST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
waterspout was located 8 miles southwest of Ben Lomond, or 10 miles
west of Santa Cruz, moving southeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Expect damage to mobile homes, roofs, and vehicles.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of West Central Santa Cruz County.

Possible waterspout over the ocean moving onshore.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 18 at 10:12AM PST until November 18 at 11:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
SVRMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern San Mateo County in northern California...

* Until 1100 AM PST.

* At 1012 AM PST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
5 miles northeast of Burlingame to over Half Moon Bay, or along a
line from 5 miles northeast of Burlingame to 10 miles southwest of
Belmont, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to
mobile homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

* Locations impacted include...
San Mateo, San Bruno, Pacifica, Burlingame, Belmont, Millbrae, Half
Moon Bay, Hillsborough, Highlands-Baywood Park, El Granada and
Highlands.
properties.instruction:
Wind damage with these storms will occur before any rain or
lightning. Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover.
Seek shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 4:58PM PST until November 18 at 7:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Plaskett burn area in...
South Central Monterey County in central California...

* Until 730 PM PST.

* At 458 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Plaskett Burn Area. Between 1.5 and 2.5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Plaskett Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Plaskett Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including
Los Burros Road.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Los Burros Road, areas near Plaskett
Creek Campground and structures along the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 7:30 PM PST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 7:30 PM PST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 18 at 8:19PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong
onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy
rainfall  expected across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.6 feet Sunday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 18 at 5:19PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 3 feet
expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet above
8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 18 at 9:46PM EST until November 19 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...East to southeast winds 20 to 25 knots and seas 5 to 8
ft, highest across the Straits of Florida.

* WHERE...Straits of Florida, and Hawk Channel from Ocean Reef
to west end of Seven Mile Bridge.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
swamped bows at reef tract mooring balls, and dragging anchors.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced boaters, especially those with smaller vessels,
should avoid operating in these conditions.
